title: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard
subtitle: A castle above the labyrinth
summary: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about an adventuring guild climbing toward a floating castle. body: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about an adventuring guild climbing toward a floating castle. The Grand Duchy of High Lagaard recruits explorers to investigate the forested Yggdrasil Labyrinth and the treasure said to lie beyond it. The player creates a party, equips it in town and enters the maze a step at a time. The destination gives the expedition a clear upward direction, while every new floor adds another place that must be understood before the next climb.

The lower screen carries a map drawn with the stylus while the first-person view shows the passage ahead. More annotation symbols allow a more detailed record than in the first game. Warp points can shorten the journey home, making their positions valuable information when the party needs rest or supplies. A map earns its usefulness through repeated visits. The player who records a turning carefully during a healthy expedition may rely on that same mark later, when the party is deciding how much danger lies between it and safety.

Ordinary encounters interrupt travel, while visible FOEs move around the labyrinth according to their own patterns. Since time advances with actions, observing a route can make it possible to pass a dangerous creature without fighting. New classes, including Gunner, War Magus and Beast, expand the choices available when building a guild. The sequel develops the original expedition rather than abandoning it: another set of specialists and clearer maps can support a better plan, but the player still has to decide when a promising journey should end with a retreat to town.
story_headings: Every step also moves a threat
